strings.d1.s0.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore
strings.d1.s0.tips: Entry to the cathedral is free (expect a queue). The Brunelleschi Pass (30 EUR) covers the dome, bell tower, baptistery and museum.
strings.d1.s1.name: Brunelleschi's Dome Climb
strings.d1.s1.tips: 463 steps. Book a timed slot weeks ahead. You climb past the frescoes to a view over the city.
strings.d1.s2.name: Battistero di San Giovanni
strings.d1.s2.tips: Ghiberti's Gates of Paradise (copy) and the mosaic ceiling. Included in the pass.
strings.d1.s3.name: Mercato Centrale Firenze
strings.d1.s3.tips: Market on the ground floor, food hall upstairs. Try lampredotto (tripe sandwich) at Nerbone and a truffle sandwich.
strings.d1.s4.name: Piazza della Signoria
strings.d1.s4.tips: An open-air sculpture museum: Loggia dei Lanzi, the Neptune Fountain and a copy of David.
strings.d1.b0.name: All'Antico Vinaio
strings.d1.b0.tips: Schiacciata sandwiches with a queue out the door. On Via dei Neri.
strings.d1.b1.name: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo
strings.d1.b1.tips: The original Gates of Paradise and Michelangelo's Pietà. Included in the pass.
strings.d2.s0.name: Galleria degli Uffizi
strings.d2.s0.tips: Botticelli's Venus, Leonardo, Caravaggio. Take the 08:15 first slot, book online (29 EUR) and allow 2.5 hours.
strings.d2.s1.name: Ponte Vecchio
strings.d2.s1.tips: The bridge of the goldsmiths, with the Vasari Corridor running above.
strings.d2.s2.name: Trattoria Sergio Gozzi
strings.d2.s2.tips: A local trattoria in San Lorenzo since 1915. Ribollita (Tuscan bread soup) and bistecca at lunch.
strings.d2.s3.name: Basilica di San Lorenzo & Medici Chapels
strings.d2.s3.tips: Michelangelo's sculptures in the New Sacristy, and the Medici tombs.
strings.d2.s4.name: Piazzale Michelangelo
strings.d2.s4.tips: The postcard view of the city at sunset. The church of San Miniato is 10 minutes further up (Gregorian chant at 17:30).
strings.d2.b0.name: Trattoria Mario
strings.d2.b0.tips: Lunch at shared tables opposite the market. Cash only.
strings.d2.b1.name: Palazzo Vecchio
strings.d2.b1.tips: The town hall and the Salone dei Cinquecento, with views from the tower.
strings.d3.s0.name: Galleria dell'Accademia
strings.d3.s0.tips: Michelangelo's David and the Prisoners. Book the 08:15 slot online.
strings.d3.s1.name: Museo di San Marco
strings.d3.s1.tips: Monastic cells frescoed by Fra Angelico. Quiet.
strings.d3.s2.name: Mercato di Sant'Ambrogio
strings.d3.s2.tips: A local market, with Cibrèo café and Trattoria da Rocco (inside the market).
strings.d3.s3.name: Basilica of Santa Croce
strings.d3.s3.tips: Tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, plus Giotto's frescoes.
strings.d3.s4.name: Scuola del Cuoio
strings.d3.s4.tips: A leather school behind Santa Croce. Watch the craftsmen at work.
strings.d3.b0.name: Trattoria da Rocco Sant'Ambrogio
strings.d3.b1.name: Museo Galileo
strings.d3.b1.tips: Scientific instruments. An alternative to Santa Croce.
strings.d4.s0.name: Palazzo Pitti Galleria Palatina
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Medici palace, with Raphael and Titian. A combined ticket with the Uffizi costs 40 EUR.
strings.d4.s1.name: Boboli Gardens
strings.d4.s1.tips: A Renaissance garden. See the Neptune pool and cross over to Bardini.
strings.d4.s2.name: Giardino Bardini
strings.d4.s2.tips: Included with the Boboli ticket. Look for the wisteria tunnel (April to May) and the view of the Duomo.
strings.d4.s3.name: Gustapizza Oltrarno
strings.d4.s3.tips: Neapolitan-style pizza near Santo Spirito. Expect a queue.
strings.d4.s4.name: Piazza Santo Spirito
strings.d4.s4.tips: The square of the artisans' quarter, with Brunelleschi's church and workshops (Via Maggio). Come for aperitivo in the evening.
strings.d4.b0.name: Il Santo Bevitore
strings.d4.b1.name: Brancacci Chapel
strings.d4.b1.tips: Masaccio's frescoes in Santa Maria del Carmine. Reserve.
strings.d5.s0.name: Piazza del Campo Siena
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by bus. A shell-shaped square, home to the Palio (2 July to 16 August).
strings.d5.s1.name: Siena Cathedral
strings.d5.s1.tips: A black-and-white striped cathedral with the Piccolomini Library and a marble floor (uncovered August to October).
strings.d5.s2.name: Torre del Mangia
strings.d5.s2.tips: A 400-step tower with views over the Campo.
strings.d5.s3.name: Osteria Le Logge Siena
strings.d5.s3.tips: Tuscan cooking next to the Campo. Try the pici pasta.
strings.d5.s4.name: San Gimignano Towers
strings.d5.s4.tips: The medieval Manhattan, with 14 towers. Stop at Gelateria Dondoli (world champion ice cream) and walk the walls at sunset.
strings.d5.b0.name: Gelateria Dondoli San Gimignano
strings.d5.b1.name: Monteriggioni
strings.d5.b1.tips: A village with circular walls. A closer alternative to San Gimignano.
strings.d6.s0.name: Greve in Chianti
strings.d6.s0.tips: The capital of Chianti, with a triangular square and Antica Macelleria Falorni.
strings.d6.s1.name: Castello di Verrazzano Wine Tour
strings.d6.s1.tips: A tour of the castle's vineyard with tasting. Reserve; go by tour or car.
strings.d6.s2.name: Castello di Verrazzano Lunch
strings.d6.s2.tips: Tuscan lunch at the vineyard, served with wine.
strings.d6.s3.name: Panzano in Chianti
strings.d6.s3.tips: Dario Cecchini's butcher village, home to the poet-butcher.
strings.d6.s4.name: Castellina in Chianti
strings.d6.s4.tips: An Etruscan tunnel and the town walls, with vineyards at sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Officina della Bistecca Dario Cecchini
strings.d6.b1.name: Badia a Passignano
strings.d6.b1.tips: An abbey and the Antinori vineyards. An alternative to Verrazzano.
strings.d7.theme: Santa Maria Novella: a light farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Novella
strings.d7.s0.tips: Masaccio's Trinity, next to the station.
strings.d7.s1.name: Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella
strings.d7.s1.tips: A pharmacy and perfumery since 1221. Good for gifts.
strings.d7.s2.name: Trattoria Sostanza
strings.d7.s2.tips: Famous for its butter chicken breast since 1869. Cash only, lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: Firenze Santa Maria Novella Station
strings.d7.s3.tips: Pisa is 1 hour away and Rome 1.5 hours. Tram T2 to the airport takes 20 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Trattoria Sabatino Oltrarno
strings.d7.b1.name: Museo Novecento
strings.d7.b1.tips: 20th-century art. An alternative to the basilica.
strings.note0: Florence is walkable (the centre is a ZTL, closed to cars). Take the bus (SITA) to Siena and San Gimignano; for Chianti, use a car or a tour. Tram T2 runs to the airport.
strings.note1: Uffizi, Accademia, dome: buy timed tickets online weeks ahead. The first Sunday is free (and crowded). Firenze Card costs 85 EUR for 72 hours.
strings.note2: November to February is quiet and 8–12°C. There are no museum queues, December brings the Christmas market, and November is olive oil harvest in Chianti.
strings.note3: Lampredotto 5 EUR, schiacciata 8 EUR, trattoria 20–30 EUR, bistecca 50–60 EUR/kg. Coperto (cover charge) 2–3 EUR, coffee at the bar 1.30 EUR.
strings.note4: Tap water is safe to drink. Cover shoulders and knees in the Duomo and churches.
strings.note5: The Vasari Corridor has reopened (reserve through the Uffizi).
